turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_supercon_train.csv: 300 real materials, columns `composition`
    (element fractions as a compact formula string) and `target` (the
    measured critical temperature Tc (K)).
  - b3_supercon_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE materials whose critical temperature
    Tc (K) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and `composition`.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST critical
temperature Tc (K), then select the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
**Reasoning:** The highest Tc values in training are cuprates — Tl/Hg/Bi-based Ba-Ca-Cu-O systems (105–137 K), especially Tl₂Ba₂CaCuO (108–123) and Bi(Pb)SrCaCuO with Cu₃ (105–111 K). Scanning the pool for analogous high‑n cuprates:

- **c034** Tl2Ba2Ca5Cu6O16 — Tl-22(n) cuprate with many Cu layers; Tl2Ba2Ca2Cu3O was 110 K, so this should be ≥110 K.
- **c046** Bi1.7Pb0.2Mo0.1Sr2Ca2Cu3O — very close to the 105–111 K Bi-2223 training entries.
- **c097** Bi1.6Pb0.4Sr2Ca3Cu3.996Ag0.004O — Bi-2223/Ag doped, similar to 91–106 K entries.
- **c084** Hg0.7Bi0.3Sr2Ca2Cu3O8.35 — Hg-based 3-Cu-layer cuprate, analogous to Hg entries at 95–130 K.
- **c044** Tl2Ba2Ca0.8Y0.2Cu1.96Co0.04O8 — close to Tl2Ba2Ca0.95Y0.05Cu1.88Co0.12O8 (85.5 K).

Other cuprates (c049, c075, c071, c017 ~Y123-type, 80–90 K; c036, c038 Tl cuprates) rank slightly below these. Non-cuprates (borocarbides, pnictides, intermetallics) are all far lower.

Final: c034, c046, c097, c084, c044
